title: Projective sheaf models from lisse residue cohomology on a weakly contractible affine
statement: Fix a prime $\ell$ and a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $R=\mathcal O_E$, uniformizer $\varpi$, and residue field $k=R/(\varpi)$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $S$ be an affine weakly contractible scheme for its small pro-etale site [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], meaning that evaluation on $S$ sends every epimorphism of sheaves of sets to a surjection. For each open subscheme $U\subseteq S$, put $B_U=\varprojlim_{n\geq1}(R/\varpi^n)_U$ [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf, def-pur-sheaf-inverse-limit]. Let $K\in D(\operatorname{Mod}(B_S))$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category, def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Assume that $K$ is derived complete for its quotient tower, meaning that the quotient maps exhibit $K$ as a derived limit of $(K\otimes^L_{B_S}(R/\varpi^n)_S)_{n\geq1}$, with its canonical reduction transitions and all terms viewed in $D(\operatorname{Mod}(B_S))$ by restriction of scalars [def-weil-derived-limit, def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars]. Assume also that its derived residue reduction $K_1=K\otimes^L_{B_S}k_S$ [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings] has locally constant [def-weil-proetale-locally-constant-sheaf] constructible cohomology sheaves (locally constant with finite-dimensional $k$-module local models) with only finitely many nonzero degrees [def-weil-proetale-constructible-sheaf, def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves], and has finite Tor amplitude locally: there are integers $a\leq b$ such that for every pro-etale $U\to S$ and every $k_U$-module sheaf $L$, the cohomology sheaves of $(K_1|_U)\otimes^L_{k_U}L$ vanish outside $[a,b]$ [def-weil-derived-tensor, def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves]. Then there is a finite disjoint open covering $S=\coprod_i U_i$ [def-weil-open-immersion] such that, for each $i$, $K|_{U_i}$ is represented by a bounded complex of $B_{U_i}$-module sheaves whose terms are direct summands of finite sums $B_{U_i}^{\oplus r}$ (each summand has inclusion and retraction maps whose composite is its identity). The differentials are arbitrary $B_{U_i}$-linear sheaf maps; no constancy of their matrix entries over $R$ is asserted.

proof.text: Apply lem-sf-residue-lisse-clopen-bases to obtain a finite disjoint open covering. On each member X, the completed pullback M is complete, X is compact and weakly contractible, all completed finite free sheaves are projective, and one ordered interval [a,b] and rank function r identify the residue cohomology with finite free sheaves. The same residue Tor interval holds on every object of X_proet.

source.place: Tag 09C3, lemma-local-structure-constructible-complex; finite-residue-field specialization of the top-degree cone induction.

proof.text: On this fixed X prove by strong induction on (b-a).toNat that M has a finite free cochain model supported in [a,b]. Apply lem-sf-complete-top-residue-cell-cone to the chosen bases, giving a distinguished triangle F[-b] -> M -> L -> F[-b+1], completeness of L, and the shortened residue bases and Tor interval.

source.place: Tag 09C3, lemma-local-structure-constructible-complex; finite-residue-field specialization of the top-degree cone induction.

proof.text: If a=b, the cone theorem says the first morphism is an isomorphism. Use the actual single complex with F=topCellIntegralFree(r b) in degree b. Its other terms are zero, identified with the free module on the empty basis. This proves the singleton-interval case, including rank zero.

source.place: Tag 09C3, lemma-local-structure-constructible-complex; finite-residue-field specialization of the top-degree cone induction.

proof.text: If a<b, (b-1-a).toNat is strictly smaller. Induction applied to L and its supplied residue bases gives a finite free model Q supported in [a,b-1]. Every term of Q is projective, by its isomorphism to a completed finite free sheaf. Transport the distinguished triangle along the induction isomorphism L ~= Q(Q).

source.place: Tag 09C3, lemma-local-structure-constructible-complex; finite-residue-field specialization of the top-degree cone induction.

proof.text: The private attachCell proof works in any abelian category: a bounded-above complex of projectives is K-projective (Mathlib CochainComplex.isKProjective_of_projective). Surjectivity of IsKProjective.Qh_map_bijective, followed by the homotopy quotient map_surjective, represents the connecting morphism by a chain map g:Q -> F[-b+1]. Rotate the distinguished triangle twice and compare its first two objects with the cone triangle of g by isoTriangleOfIso12. Shift the resulting third-object isomorphism by -1, obtaining Q(Cone(g)[-1]) ~= M. The literal cone projections give its terms Q^q for q != b and F in degree b; the remaining terms vanish. Thus the resulting model is finite free and supported in [a,b]. All these comparisons are proved in Lean, without a new proof obligation.

source.place: Tag 09C3, lemma-local-structure-constructible-complex; finite-residue-field specialization of the top-degree cone induction.

proof.text: Apply the induction on each member. Reindex each finite free sheaf from ULift(Fin N) to Fin N by Sigma.whiskerEquiv. In the abelian sheaf category the finite coproduct is isomorphic to the finite product through biproduct.isoCoproduct and biproduct.isoProduct. Compose with each term isomorphism and use its hom and inv as the required inclusion and retraction. These maps compose to the identity. The empty covering is allowed, and neither the induction nor the cone calculation constrains the differentials to constant matrices.

lean.statement: theorem residue_lisse_projective_models (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : IsAffine S) (hweak : (Scheme.ProEt.topology S).IsWeaklyContractible.{u + 1} (Scheme.ProEt.mk (𝟙 S))) (K : DerivedCategory (integralTowerModules.{u, u} l E S)) (hcomplete : IsDerivedCompleteUnrestricted l E S K) (hresidue : intrinsicFiniteTorsionConstructible l E 1 (by omega) S ((scalarReductionDerivedExtension.{u, u} l E S 0).obj K)) (hlisse : ∀ q : ℤ, IsLocallyConstantProEtaleModuleSheaf S (Padic.coefficientExtensionRing l E 1) ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (proEtaleRingModules S (proEtaleConstantRing S (Padic.coefficientExtensionRing l E 1))) q).obj ((scalarReductionDerivedExtension.{u, u} l E S 0).obj K))) (hTor : HasFiniteProEtaleTorAmplitude S (Padic.coefficientExtensionRing l E 1) ((scalarReductionDerivedExtension.{u, u} l E S 0).obj K)) : ∃ (n : ℕ) (U : Fin n → S.Opens), (⨆ i, U i) = ⊤ ∧ Pairwise (fun i j ↦ Disjoint (U i) (U j)) ∧ ∀ i : Fin n, ∃ (P : CochainComplex (integralTowerModules.{u, u} l E (U i).toScheme) ℤ) (a b : ℤ), a ≤ b ∧ P.IsStrictlyGE a ∧ P.IsStrictlyLE b ∧ (∀ r : ℤ, ∃ (N : ℕ) (ι : P.X r ⟶ ∏ᶜ fun _ : Fin N ↦ SheafOfModules.unit (completedIntegralCoefficientSheafUnrestricted l E (U i).toScheme)) (ρ : (∏ᶜ fun _ : Fin N ↦ SheafOfModules.unit (completedIntegralCoefficientSheafUnrestricted l E (U i).toScheme)) ⟶ P.X r), ι ≫ ρ = 𝟙 _) ∧ Nonempty ((integralDerivedPullback l E (U i).ι).obj K ≅ DerivedCategory.Q.obj P)
